title: Microsoft Teams: connect a meeting to an existing Planner plan
summary: Hold: the table says Facilitator automation is not documented, although Microsoft documents an app-state PowerShell operation. The roadmap and notice facts are accurate, but the page should also report Microsoft's conflicting Facilitator navigation instructions rather than presenting one route without qualification.

claims.quote: With this capability, users can now connect Teams meetings to existing Planner plans, so all related tasks across meetings can be tracked in one place.

claims.claim: Teams meetings currently automatically create separate Planner plans for meeting tasks.
claims.quote: Currently, Teams meetings automatically create separate Planner plans for meeting-related tasks

claims.claim: Tasks for one long-running initiative can become scattered across multiple auto-generated plans.
claims.quote: when teams use meetings as their primary collaboration surface for long-running initiatives, tasks from the same project can become scattered across multiple auto-generated plans.

claims.claim: The Facilitator page documents Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block.
claims.quote: select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. ... In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.
claims.fix: Add to the Facilitator row note: 'Microsoft pages disagree on navigation: the Facilitator setup page gives Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Allow or Block; the app-management page says Facilitator is managed under Teams apps > Built-in Teams agents > Facilitator > Edit availability, with availability set to no one to restrict access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/manage-apps#manage-built-in-teams-agents. Do not silently replace one documented route with the other.

claims.claim: Facilitator is allowed by default.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.
claims.fix: Qualify the default statement in controls[0].note: 'The Facilitator setup page says Facilitator is allowed by default, but is also blocked if all apps are blocked for the organisation.'

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation for controlling Facilitator availability.
claims.quote: This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app. ... Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <String> [-IsBlocked <Boolean>] ... -IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.
claims.fix: Do not render 'Not yet documented' for a documented but ambiguous operation. Set controls[0].api to kind 'powershell', call 'Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean>', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp'. Retain the warning that its -IsBlocked $true example is labelled as unblocking, without prescribing a Boolean value for blocking. Describe it as the documented Teams app-state operation, not as a verified call for the alternative Built-in Teams agents route.

claims.claim: The Update-M365TeamsApp reference labels its -IsBlocked $true example as unblocking.
claims.quote: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true ... Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams/update-m365teamsapp to sources, titled 'Update-M365TeamsApp'. The row calls it a cited reference, but the current page has no citation to it.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app for the organisation.
claims.quote: go to Teams apps > Manage apps. ... To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false is the documented organisation-wide Planner disable operation.
claims.quote: If you're a global admin and you want to turn off Microsoft Planner for your organization, you can use Windows PowerShell. ... Set-PlannerConfiguration -IsPlannerAllowed $false
claims.fix: Add to controls[1].note: 'The reference is internally inconsistent: its title and introduction describe disabling Planner, but the sentence introducing this command says it turns off Outlook calendar sync.' Keep the documented command rather than inferring a different operation.
